learningObjective: Diagnose a race condition in a CUDA kernel from symptoms (non-deterministic output, small numerical drift across runs) and identify the missing synchronization primitive.

canonicalClaims.claim: Shared-memory reductions across an entire block require __syncthreads() between phases (load → reduce, and between reduction iterations). Without those barriers, threads may read partially-updated shared memory, producing non-deterministic results.
conditions: Block size larger than a single warp.
Compute capability supports independent warp scheduling (Volta+).
nonImplications: Does not imply barriers eliminate all non-determinism (e.g., cross-block atomicAdd order still matters).
Does not imply barriers are free; they add small latency but are required.

misconceptions.claim: Threads within a warp are always in lockstep, so __syncthreads is unnecessary at the warp level.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Since Volta, independent warp scheduling means intra-warp synchronization also requires explicit primitives (__syncwarp) for correctness.
Atomic-associativity concerns are cross-block, not intra-block; intra-block races come from missing barriers.

misconceptions.claim: Uninitialized shared memory contains device garbage.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Shared memory contents are undefined until written; the block only reads what it wrote.
It is a required correctness primitive for shared-memory-based algorithms.
